To determine who was allowed to participate in the Greek democratic process (specifically in Athens, as described in Pericles' Funeral Oration by Thucydides) during the time period of the text:

Step 1: Understand the historical context of Athenian democracy in the 5th century B.C.E.
Step 2: Recall the qualifications for political participation (voting in the assembly, holding public office) in classical Athens. 
Step 3: In ancient Athens, citizenship and political rights were restricted to adult males. Women, enslaved people, resident aliens (metics), and children were excluded from the democratic process.
Step 4: Furthermore, citizenship generally required being born of citizen parents (and later, under Pericles' citizenship law of 451 B.C.E., both parents had to be Athenians), making them citizens by birth.
Step 5: Review the given options in light of this historical fact:
- (A) All adult men born within the geographic boundaries of the state (too broad, as it would include non-citizens living there).
- (B) All adult men and women born within the geographic boundaries of the state (incorrect because women were excluded).
- (C) All adult men who were citizens of the state by birth (correct, as political participation was limited to adult male citizens).
- (D) All adult men and women who were citizens of the state by birth (incorrect because women could not participate).

Final answer: C
